title: Invariant coverage tax: totality versus proportionality

completion_criteria.text: Map the enforcement chain end to end and write it down: registry, coverage entry, checker modes, CI wiring, and exactly where the seventeen-row obligation is generated
Measure the real cost rather than assert it: what a full coverage entry actually costs on a low-risk change, and how that scales as the registry grows past seventeen ids
Settle against M1 and M2 as ratified: does proportional coverage necessarily reintroduce the self-selected allowlist M2 forbids, or is there a form that does not
Choose one resolution on robustness first then simplicity, record the decision, and name explicitly what it gives up
Implement it with red-before/green-after receipts and its own coverage entry, then ship one PR via pr-create

spine.active_goal: Implement c5: ship the paths-only inert predicate ratified in 0273, with receipts, its own coverage entry, and one PR.
spine.next_step: START c5 in a fresh session, implementing 0273. Add inert_when {paths} to registry entries; evaluate it in scripts/invariant-coverage-check.mjs against the diff it already computes; structurally reject inert_when on M3/M4/M5; have the checker write each inert row's check text naming the paths evaluated and the glob matched. Owed: red-before/green-after test, halt-on-unclassifiable test, an inertness mutation, loud failure when no base resolves. Then its own entry and one PR via pr-create.
spine.last_session: Ran c2 as a real five-arm experiment and ratified c4. Measured 76.3k fixed plus 2,298 per row (R2 0.995); retired wall-clock as unmeasurable after a replicate landed 2.7x apart. c3 settled as the premise of the c4 choice. Nothing was committed.

open_risks.text: Keep the inert polarity negative, so the basis holds only when every changed path matches a declared glob — flip it to positive matching and the gate stops halting on the unclassifiable, which is the ratified rule evaded rather than satisfied

Bar M3, M4 and M5 from carrying inert_when structurally rather than by convention — M4 forcing a look is the only thing that caught the OptionA truncation, and nothing in a solo repo would notice that catch quietly disappearing
Write the inert globs narrowly and expect no reviewer to catch a wide one — this is a solo repo, so an over-broad glob silently converts a real check into a proved-inert row

An inert basis cannot be evaluated when no base commit resolves and must fail loudly there — that is a live behavior change from what 0264 shipped for push mode, so it needs a test rather than an argument
The checker is itself a gate, so the halt-on-unclassifiable, red-on-parent and deployed-artifact obligations all apply to changing it — a gate that exempts itself proves nothing

key_decisions.title: Invariant coverage cost measured: 76.3k fixed plus 2,298 tokens per row, linear and unbounded
Adopt the registry-declared inert predicate, paths-only, with M3/M4/M5 structurally barred from carrying it
Hand-authored inert globs are not survivable; the declarable class must be enforced by a checker kind rule

out_of_scope: Moving the verdict into the PR body - pr-create's flag set is closed and its values cap at 200 characters, which is why M1 puts the verdict in a committed artifact
Any resolution needing a second reviewer, a bot account, or org-level infrastructure - this is a solo owner-held repo
